role: Deputy care home manager (registered nurse) auditing one resident's completed medication round record the following morning
setting: A residential and nursing care home keeps an electronic medication administration record. Each morning the deputy manager audits completed rounds one resident at a time. Each record joins the resident's details, current prescriptions and amendments, the doses signed during the round, item stock counts, round details with open queries and post-dose observations, and a short error history. The reviewer must decide whether the record closes cleanly, needs correcting, is held for confirmation, or triggers an incident report or clinical escalation.

dose_mismatch.instructions: A dose given this round differed from the prescription in force.

stock_reconciles.instructions: Every item's closing stock reconciles with opening, receipts and signed doses.

criteria.true: Each closing count equals expected after recorded movements
criteria.false: At least one closing count differs from expected

next_step.instructions: What should the reviewer do with this round record next?

criteria.sign_off: No discrepancies found; record is complete and can close.
criteria.correct_and_close: Recording slip only; amend with annotation, then close record.
criteria.hold: One open query must be answered before outcome is decided.
criteria.report_incident: Confirmed error on an ordinary drug; file internal incident report.
criteria.clinical_escalation: Confirmed error on time-critical or high-risk drug; seek GP advice.

open_discrepancies.instructions: How many items still have an unresolved discrepancy after review?
criteria: No item has an unresolved discrepancy
Exactly one item has an unresolved discrepancy
Two or three items have unresolved discrepancies
Four or more items have unresolved discrepancies

error_severity.instructions: How severe is the worst error found in this round?
criteria: None: every dose correct or validly withheld
Documentation: dose correct but signature or code missing
Timing: correct dose given over 60 minutes late
Dose: ordinary drug omitted, duplicated or wrong strength
Critical: time-critical drug omitted, duplicated or wrong strength

factors.name: dose_mismatch_type
factors.description: Whether and how units_given in an administration entry departs from the prescribed dose_units for that item

factors.name: prescription_change_documented
factors.description: Whether a dated amendment with an order reference makes the apparently mismatched dose correct for this round

factors.name: omission_count
factors.description: Number of scheduled doses with no administration entry or a not-given code

factors.name: omission_reason_valid
factors.description: Whether omissions carry a code backed elsewhere, such as resident status hospital or a withhold order

factors.name: late_minutes
factors.description: Largest gap in minutes between scheduled and given_at time across the round

factors.name: time_critical_affected
factors.description: Whether the item carrying the worst error is flagged time_critical or high_risk in prescriptions

factors.name: stock_variance
factors.description: Closing count minus expected count for the most discrepant item; zero means reconciled

factors.name: stock_variance_explained
factors.description: Whether a witnessed wasted or returned movement in stock accounts for the variance

factors.name: signature_gaps
factors.description: Number of administration entries missing initials, or missing second initials for controlled drugs

factors.name: unit_expression_decoy
factors.description: How a correct dose is expressed: same units as prescribed, or an equivalent split such as two 5 mg tablets for 10 mg

factors.name: post_dose_obs_reassuring
factors.description: Whether a post-dose observation (blood glucose, pulse, INR due date) after the error lies within normal range

factors.name: pending_query
factors.description: Open query on the round whose answer would change the outcome

factors.name: prior_errors_30d
factors.description: Count of medication incidents for this resident in the past 30 days; context only, never decisive

factors.name: item_count
factors.description: Number of prescribed items on the round, setting how many places discrepancies can hide

sections.name: resident
sections.description: Resident id, room, dob, weight_kg, allergies list, status and status_since date

sections.name: prescriptions
sections.description: List of items: item_id, drug, strength_mg, form, dose_units, times, prn, time_critical, high_risk, controlled, changes list

sections.name: administrations
sections.description: List of entries: item_id, scheduled, given_at, units_given, strength_mg_used, code, initials, second_initials

sections.name: stock
sections.description: Per item: opening, received, wasted, wasted_witnessed, returned, closing

sections.name: round
sections.description: Round_id, date, slot, started, finished, staff_on, open_queries list, post_dose_obs list

sections.name: history
sections.description: Errors_30d, refusals_7d, last_audit date, last_audit_passed boolean

rendering_notes: prescriptions holds item_count items; administrations has one entry per scheduled dose. dose_mismatch_type shows only as units_given or strength_mg_used differing from the matching prescription item, or a second entry for the same item_id and scheduled time; it is never labelled. prescription_change_documented appears as a changes entry {effective, new_dose_units, order_ref, authorised_by_role}; when false, either no change exists or the effective date falls after the round date or order_ref is null. omission_count shows as missing entries or code values R, H, W, N or O with units_given 0; omission_reason_valid is true only when the code is supported elsewhere (H with resident.status hospital and status_since before the round; W with a changes entry carrying a withhold order_ref); a code alone does not count. late_minutes is derived from scheduled versus given_at; place values near 60 regularly to create boundary cases. time_critical_affected is the time_critical or high_risk flag on the erroneous item. stock_variance shows as closing differing from opening + received - wasted - returned - doses signed; stock_variance_explained true adds a wasted or returned amount equal to the gap with wasted_witnessed true; a wasted amount with wasted_witnessed false is a contested case. signature_gaps shows as null initials, or null second_initials on a controlled item. unit_expression_decoy: equivalent_split records units_given 2 with strength_mg_used 5 against a 10 mg prescription, which is correct and not a mismatch. post_dose_obs_reassuring appears in round.post_dose_obs as a numeric value within or outside normal range for its type, with no range label. pending_query appears in round.open_queries with type, raised timestamp and item_id; none means an empty list. prior_errors_30d, refusals_7d and last_audit_passed are decoys giving context and never decide an answer. Decoys also include allergies (never matching a prescribed drug), weight_kg and staff_on. No field states an error, severity, discrepancy, reconciliation result or recommended action; records contain no free-text fields, only codes, numbers, ISO timestamps, booleans and nulls.
